claims.text: NbTaTiV is a refractory BCC high-entropy alloy.
The NbTaTiV alloy has a grain size of 200–400 μm.
The initial NbTaTiV alloy has significant compositional fluctuations.
The compositional fluctuations in the initial alloy produce severe lattice distortion.
High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in refractory BCC alloys are primarily governed by the extent of compositional lattice distortion.
Compositional lattice distortion induces wavy dislocation cores or lines.
Severe lattice distortion displaces edge-dislocation cores from their neutral planes.
Wavy dislocation lines reduce the mobility of <111>{110} edge dislocations.
Reduced edge-dislocation mobility at high temperature enhances ductility or toughness.
An alloy with greater lattice distortion will have greater high-temperature toughness than a less-distorted control.
An alloy with greater lattice distortion will have a reduced rate of plastic strain relative to a less-distorted control.
The cited NbTaTiV alloy remains a single BCC solid solution through 900°C.
NbTaTiV has been compression-tested at 500°C, 700°C, and 900°C at a strain rate of 1 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹.
The mechanism should apply primarily between 500°C and 900°C.
The mechanism should apply to refractory BCC alloys having similar valence-electron concentrations and grain sizes.
In lower-heterogeneity conventional BCC alloys, screw or otherwise less-modified dislocation mobility dominates high-temperature deformation.
Processing or compositional tuning can create a more ordered, less-distorted comparison alloy while retaining a comparable grain structure and microstructure.
TEM can distinguish the predicted wavy dislocation pattern between the high-distortion alloy and the control.

contradictions.description: Both materials are specified to be deformed at the same controlled strain rate of approximately 1 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹, yet the prediction calls for a reduced rate of plastic strain in the high-distortion alloy. Under imposed strain-rate control, plastic strain amount, stress response, or creep rate would need to be distinguished from the externally prescribed deformation rate.

The mechanism describes inhibited dislocation mobility as producing enhanced ductility, while the predicted outcome is reduced plastic strain. Enhanced ductility normally entails increased plastic-strain capacity, so the intended distinction between strain rate, accumulated plastic strain, and strain to failure is unresolved.
